cards.front: Recall a key point about World Cinema & Audiences
cards.back: Audience reception of global film is shaped by cultural context: viewers from different backgrounds interpret the same film differently based on their own values and experiences.

cards.front: Recall a key point about World Cinema & Audiences
cards.back: Subtitles preserve the original language performance and cultural authenticity but require active reading and can distract from visual composition.

cards.front: Recall a key point about World Cinema & Audiences
cards.back: Dubbing allows viewers to focus entirely on the image but replaces original vocal performances and can flatten cultural specificity through translation choices.

cards.front: Recall a key point about World Cinema & Audiences
cards.back: Cultural bridging occurs when a film from one culture resonates with audiences from another, often through universal themes such as family, love or justice.

cards.front: Recall a key point about World Cinema & Audiences
cards.back: Some films achieve crossover success by blending local cultural specificity with globally recognised genres or narrative structures.

cards.front: Recall a key point about World Cinema & Audiences
cards.back: UK audiences' engagement with world cinema has been transformed by streaming platforms that subtitle international content and make it readily accessible.

cards.front: Recall a key point about World Cinema & Audiences
cards.back: Audience positioning in global film differs from Hollywood because viewers may lack cultural knowledge that the film assumes, requiring more active interpretation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about World Cinema & Audiences
cards.back: Cultural context affects how audiences read genre: a horror film from Japan draws on different folk traditions and fears than one from the UK or US.

cards.front: Recall a key point about World Cinema & Audiences
cards.back: The debate between subtitling and dubbing involves cultural respect, accessibility and commercial considerations, with different countries favouring different approaches.

cards.front: Recall a key point about World Cinema & Audiences
cards.back: Film festivals and critics play a crucial role in guiding UK audiences towards world cinema, providing cultural context that aids interpretation and appreciation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about World Cinema & Audiences
cards.back: Global film can challenge ethnocentric assumptions by presenting perspectives and storytelling traditions that differ from dominant Western conventions.

cards.front: Recall a key point about World Cinema & Audiences
cards.back: Audience demographics for world cinema in the UK skew towards older, more educated viewers, though streaming is gradually broadening the audience base.
